item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-13

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-13 03:08 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-13

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains a very high-activity project: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24h, with 335 open/active issues and 314 open PRs. Throughput is strong — 165 issues closed and 186 PRs merged/closed in the same window. Two releases landed, both heavily focused on update recovery, handoff reliability, and Windows/macOS install paths. Health is mixed: maintainers are shipping recovery fixes and closing high-severity session/crash items, but multiple P0 update, Windows service, memory-leak, and disk-growth issues remain open. Overall: active and responsive, with update/install reliability as the dominant risk area.

2. Releases

Release Type Key Changes Breaking / Migration Notes
v2026.10.5-beta.2 Beta openclaw update settles stale handoff leases, completed receipts, and legacy 2026.9.8 recovery records instead of stopping on update-recovery-pending; keeps service heap limit and webhook listeners; handles Windows short-* paths (release note truncated). No explicit breaking changes in supplied notes. Migration focus: stalled/legacy update recovery.
v2026.10.2 Stable-channel upgrade First upgrade from stable 2026.10.1 now completes cleanly; successful in-place updates no longer end in errors; Windows, cloned-filesystem, and private-Node update paths finish instead of stalling or rolling back (#168849, #169031). No explicit breaking changes in supplied notes. Migration focus: 2026.10.1 upgrades and in-place update recovery.

3. Project Progress

  • 186 PRs merged/closed and 165 issues closed in the last 24h.
  • Visible closed PRs in the top activity slice:
    • #170497 — restore original Control UI startup performance budgets.
    • #170533 — consolidate chat and Solid presentation paths.
  • Closed issues show progress across crash, session, update, and model-correctness areas:
    • #137729 — unguarded .trim() crash fix pattern.
    • #157126 — claude-cli MCP bridge request-scope issue.
    • #167506 — deleted temporary handoff DB blocking update recovery.
    • #69118 — Claude CLI group-channel session reset.
    • #158936 — macOS readiness watchdog restart loop.
    • #168750 — update activation Doctor failure.
    • #127239 — context-window fallback to hardcoded 200k.
    • #9986 — model fallback on context length exceeded.
    • #119692 — MiniMax-M3 usage-accounting drop.
    • #95746 — memory-core dreaming context exhaustion.
    • #39811 — unvalidated model names.
    • #164214 — package publication recovery stuck in publishing.
  • Open PRs advancing major themes: update recovery, Doctor repairs, gateway responsiveness, CLI request-scope isolation, secrets input safety, Control UI Solid migration, plugin runtime control, memory-wiki status, and session/transcript authority.

4. Community Hot Topics

Most Active Issues

Rank Issue Comments Underlying Need
1 #159356 — llama.cpp manager reports ready while embedding child exits; HTTP 500 26 Child-process health checks and memory-pressure diagnostics for embedding stacks.
2 #159662 — prepared-model-catalog.worker.js unbounded memory leak, ~4–5 GB/h 22 Urgent memory-leak fix independent of provider/plugin config.
3 #160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins 20 Non-blocking plugin capture / event-loop starvation fix.
4 #50093 — WhatsApp backfill missed messages after reconnection 20 Channel reconnection recovery and message-loss prevention.
5 #97616 — unreaped hook/tool child processes and zombie accumulation 18 Process reaping and long-running runtime degradation fix.
6 #78308 — MCP tool-call channel-mediated approval / consent envelope 18 Security and consent gating for MCP side effects.
7 #137729 — unguarded .trim() crash in transcript replay/error classification 14 Defensive coding; closed.
8 #157126 — claude-cli MCP bridge inherits first request scope 14 Correct request-scope isolation; closed, with related PR work.
9 #156112 — openclaw update fails at global install swap 14 Updater reliability when direct npm install -g succeeds.
10 #114414 — dated TODO sweep 13 Maintainability/tech-debt cleanup.
11 #146860 — Windows managed update handoff cannot obtain process-start identity 12 Windows Scheduled Task / InteractiveToken update reliability.
12 #101929 — context-overflow precheck over-counts 2.3–2.6x 12 Accurate token accounting to avoid false truncation recovery.

Hot PRs

PR comment counts were not supplied in the snapshot; the following are high-signal PRs from the top activity slice.

  • #170534 — fix silent turn endings without fabricated answers; XL, P2, merge risks.
  • #169299 — Doctor prioritizes unresolved findings and explains repairs.
  • #166782 — keep Gateway responsive during reply-tagged streams.
  • #157144 — CLI bridge tool calls in their own run request scope; incorporated into main via #165432.
  • #167250 — prevent malformed UTF-8 from overwriting stored secrets.
  • #168368 — Mattermost agent buttons render as plain text.
  • #170527 — trigger model fallback for provider-wrapped errors.
  • #170548 — keep manual cron runs from losing tool access.
  • #169172 — tool-call text no longer leaks into chat output when chunks split a marker.
  • #170553 — prevent memory-wiki status timeouts on large vaults.
  • #169848 — lightContext ignored by CLI-backend subagents.
  • #170152 — let plugins steer a session’s active run.
  • #170555 — join lifecycle publication during Gateway shutdown.
  • #170536 — stop rechecking qualified target absence in sessions.
  • #169692 — render New Session with Solid.
  • #170387 — port shared pickers, dialogs, and toast to Solid 2.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by supplied severity. “Fix PR” reflects visible labels/linked PRs in the snapshot.

P0 / Critical

Issue Problem Fix PR Status
#159662 Unbounded memory leak in prepared-model-catalog.worker.js, ~4–5 GB/h No visible fix PR.
#160959 Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) No new fix PR.
#156112 openclaw update fails at global install swap while direct npm install succeeds Manual-only; no visible fix PR.
#146860 Windows managed update handoff stalls with InteractiveToken Scheduled Task No visible fix PR.
#158390 Plugin-captures tmp dirs never GC’d; disk fills indefinitely No new fix PR.
#167652 Windows Gateway hangs after 2026.9.9 upgrade despite Doctor verified restart Needs live repro; no fix.
#160060 Windows Gateway silently dies ~54 min after standby thaw No fix.
#166894 Gateway restart hangs 30+ min to 2h on Windows multi-agent installs No fix.
#138560 Windows Control UI update aborts with managed-service-handoff-failed No fix.
#153426 MEMORY.md / USER.md permanently excluded by provenance ratchet No fix.

P1 / High

Issue Problem Fix PR Status
#97616 Unreaped hook/tool child processes cause zombie accumulation No fix.
#101929 Context-overflow precheck over-counts ~2.3–2.6x vs billed usage No fix.
#168955 Startup regression in 2026.10.1: ready ~1030s vs ~410s on Windows No fix.
#154891 Failed/rolled-back config hot-reload bricks unrelated plugins until restart No fix.
#132303 agents.list[].tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend Security; no fix.
#126950 Telegram opaque callback payloads silently dropped No fix.
#128916 Errored message-tool-only runs end silent No fix.
#156353 Chat fails after plugin reload with transcript admission identity mismatch No fix.
#77249 Slack reconnect supervisor hangs on zombie WSS No fix.
#125826 Discord voice replies double-spoken and double-written No fix.

New / Recently Updated

  • #170331 — beta.2 update candidate config read exits 1 and leaves systemd unit unchanged.
  • #170332 — beta update continues after live state DB changes during original-state capture.
  • #164394 — Control UI WebChat transcript jitters continuously.
  • #108379 — duplicate assistant generation for Xiaomi MiMo.
  • #168413 — memory.search.extraPaths content never recalled; stale reindex lock.
  • #99659 — OpenClaw OOM-killed after companion app connected.

Potential Fix PRs in Queue

  • #170527 — model fallback for provider-wrapped errors (fixes #170388).
  • #170548 — cron manual runs keep tool access (related #170470).
  • #170534 — silent turn endings without fabricated answers (related #170147, #150539).
  • #166782 — Gateway responsive during reply-tagged streams (closes #166781).
  • #169172 — tool-call text leak fix (fixes #169161).
  • #170553 — memory-wiki status timeout fix (closes #170466).
  • #169848 — lightContext for CLI subagents (closes #169704).
  • #167250 / #167251 — malformed UTF-8 secret/model input safety.
  • #157144 — CLI bridge request scope (incorporated via #165432; related #157126).
  • #170556 — worker transcript authority.
  • #170555 — Gateway shutdown lifecycle publication.
  • #169299 — Doctor repair/reporting improvements.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Status Likely Signal
#50093 — WhatsApp backfill missed messages P1, stale, needs product decision Channel reliability and missed-message recovery.
#78308 — MCP channel-mediated approval / consent envelope P2 security Consent/approval pipeline for MCP side effects.
#16670 — onboarding wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup P2, 2 👍 Better first-run memory configuration.
#76493 — allow SecretRef objects in mcp.servers[].env P2, 4 👍 Secret indirection and secure MCP configuration.
#111143 — pin plugin tabs in Control UI sidebar P3, 1 👍 UI customization for plugin surfaces.
#114414 — dated TODO sweep P3 Maintainability/tech-debt reduction.
#169254 — promote JSON filter/delete fields to columns P3 PostgreSQL portability and data-model cleanup.

Closed feature signals: #9986 model fallback on context length exceeded, #39811 model-name validation, #127239 real context-window catalog values, and #119692 MiniMax-M3 usage accounting.

Prediction: The next beta/stable line will likely continue the update-recovery and Windows/macOS handoff theme. After that, the strongest roadmap signals are Control UI Solid migration, plugin runtime steering/GC, memory/embedding onboarding, MCP approval/SecretRef security, and channel message-recovery reliability.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Update/install frustration is the top pain point. 7. Trend Signals

  1. Updaters/installers are now first-class agent infrastructure.
    OpenClaw, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw all show pain around updates, install handoff, stale PIDs, file locks, and recovery. Developers should treat update/rollback as a core subsystem, not packaging glue.

  2. Memory, context, and RAG are becoming the durable differentiator.
    OpenClaw’s memory leaks/exclusions, ZeroClaw’s memory parity/RAG corpus, QwenPaw’s context compaction, and Hermes’ remote memory/session needs point to memory durability, provenance, and prompt-cache efficiency as core requirements.

  3. Multi-agent orchestration is moving from ad hoc config to protocol.
    ZeroClaw’s A2A/RFC/swarm work, OpenClaw’s multi-agent restart/session authority issues, and Hermes’ remote/local hybrid request show demand for first-class agent-to-agent messaging, durable turns, and session ownership.

  4. Observability and cost accounting must be correct and privacy-aware.
    Hermes’ Langfuse duplicate cluster, ZeroClaw’s cost-tab issues, OpenClaw’s usage/context accounting bugs, and QwenPaw’s Langfuse tool-observation gap indicate that traces, costs, and masking are production requirements.

  5. Security/consent is expanding beyond API keys.
    MCP approvals, SecretRef, tools.deny enforcement, pairing tokens, scoped logs, trace masking, and BYO provider keys are recurring demands. Consent gating for tool side effects is becoming a platform feature.

  6. Cross-platform Windows/desktop reliability is a competitive risk.
    OpenClaw and QwenPaw both have Windows-specific P0/high issues: service hangs, file locks, stale PID handling, log rotation. Agent developers must account for Windows process, file, and service semantics.

  7. Channel/message reliability remains core UX.
    WhatsApp backfill, Telegram DM routing, Discord voice duplication, Slack WSS hangs, DingTalk media, and multi-device sync all appear across projects. Message-loss prevention and reconnection recovery are not edge cases.

  8. Silent failures are especially damaging.
    OpenClaw silent turn endings, QwenPaw silent empty completion and binary corruption, ZeroClaw dropped elicitations and false-success cron — users lose trust when agents fail without clear signals.

  9. Modularity and self-hosting demand is rising.
    Users want BYO keys, reverse-proxy subpaths, separate channels from core, plugin hot reload/unload, reduced-effects modes, and NAS/Docker support. “Don’t ship what I don’t use” is a real security and operational preference.

  10. For AI agent developers, the build checklist is clear:
    Recoverable updates, supervised processes, durable memory with provenance, protocol-level multi-agent support, accurate cost/observability, consent-gated tools, cross-platform service handling, and explicit failure surfacing.

Bottom line: OpenClaw leads on scale, breadth, and release throughput, but its unresolved P0 reliability items are the ecosystem’s most visible risk. Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw are iterating quickly in differentiated niches, while IronClaw remains a low-activity evaluation signal. The next phase of competition will likely be decided by update/install reliability, memory/RAG durability, multi-agent protocols, observability correctness, and Windows/desktop trust.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. (The most recent release event was PR #8121, which was closed/merged — QwenPaw Creator 1.3.0 → 2.0.1 with controlled media production, discussed in Section 3.)

3. Project Progress

Four PRs were merged/closed today:

  • [PR #8188] fix(approval): preserve decisions and handle timeout races — Closes #8105, the long-standing bug where tool approval always resolved to "reject." Root cause was a race: decisions completed before the tool entered its wait state were lost. This is the highest-impact fix of the day. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8188
  • [PR #8121] feat(creator): release 2.0.1 with controlled media production (size/XXXL) — Ships the QwenPaw Creator plugin bump 1.3.0 → 2.0.1, carrying only post-upstream-release plugin work. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8121
  • [PR #8193] fix(context): reclaim active results earlier and verify overflow recovery — Improves context compaction so long active turns stop accumulating recoverable tool output beyond the trigger threshold. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8193
  • [Issue #8073] V2.2.2.beta4 unable to access conversation page on LAN — Closed; a regression affecting LAN clients opening the chat page. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8073

Features advanced but still open: reverse-proxy basename support (#8197), per-chat approval level persistence (#8182), coding-CLI management endpoints (#8156), plugin hot reload/rollback (#7565), and the "reduced effects" console tier (#8137).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count in the last 24h:

  1. #8174 — web_search Tavily provider has no API-key config surface (4 comments) — Keyless-only anonymous mode makes paid Tavily quota unusable and gives no clean fallback on 401/429/432. A first-time contributor already opened the fix, PR #8204. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8174
  2. #7016 — 工具调用 404 (Tool call not found on /offload) (4 comments) — Streaming sessions repeatedly hit a 404 on the offload endpoint. Open since 2026-08-14, still without a linked fix PR. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/7016
  3. #8172 — Console intermittent silent empty completion (3 comments) — A run finishes in ~1s with empty output and the model is never called, only on the embedded PawApp console channel. High severity, no fix PR yet. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8172

Underlying needs: users are pushing toward production-grade self-hosting (custom API keys, reverse-proxy subpaths, multi-provider web_search, server-side persistence) and desktop reliability, while the repeated 404/silent-completion reports point to fragility in the streaming/run lifecycle for embedded and remote clients.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all open unless noted):

# Issue Severity Fix PR?
1 #8172 Console silent empty completion — model never invoked, no reply rendered (v2.2.0 Docker/NAS) Critical (silent data/UX failure) ❌ None
2 #8179 Installing a skill from GitHub silently corrupts binary files (all non-UTF-8 bytes → U+FFFD; images/fonts broken) High (silent data corruption) ✅ PR #8198
3 #8206 Project deletion always fails on Windows once creator.log is open (WinError 5 on directory rename) High ❌ None
4 #8194 qwenpaw-creator startup hook aborts on stale PID — os.kill(pid, 0) raises SystemError, not caught by except OSError High (app won't start) ✅ PR #8196
5 #8184 Doom-loop gate kills legitimate task-authorized polling; cron then records false success after termination High (wrong state + silent failure) ✅ PR #8192
6 #8185 desktop.log never rotates on Windows (sidecar tee handle defeats rotating handler) Medium (disk exhaustion over time) ❌ None
7 #8186 Message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling, snapping back for ~1.6s Medium (UX) ✅ PR #8201
8 #7016 Tool-call 404 loop on /offload during streaming Medium (open since Aug) ❌ None
9 #8202 A message sent on one device is invisible on the other until the turn finishes Medium (multi-device UX) ✅ PR #8203
10 #8105 Tool approval buttons both execute "reject" High — CLOSED ✅ ✅ PR #8188 (merged)

Notable pattern: five of today's ten issues have a same-or-next-day fix PR, indicating strong contributor-to-maintainer velocity. The two Windows creator-plugin failures (#8206, #8194) share a root theme — Windows file/process semantics not accounted for — and may merit a consolidated hardening pass.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Requested features (with implementation status):

  • Configurable web_search providers — Tavily API-key surface (#8174, PR #8204) and Firecrawl as a third provider (#8199, PR #8200). Strong signal that multi-provider, BYO-key web search lands soon.
  • Reverse-proxy subpath support — configurable console basename (#8177, PR #8197); important for self-hosted multi-service domains.
  • Console "reduced effects" tier (#8135, PR #8137) — GPU load reduction on integrated graphics; positions Console for lower-end/NAS hardware.
  • Server-side per-chat approval mode (#8182) — moves approval level off browser localStorage for cross-device consistency.
  • Model pool deletion (#8195) — only enable/disable exists; deprecated models cannot be purged.
  • Coding-CLI management endpoints for worker containers (#8156) — manage qwen-code/opencode model and config per worker.
  • Decision model type + JEV provider (#8205) — backward-compatible model_type (chat/decision) hinting at upcoming routing/structured-decision features.
  • Nested/categorised skill directories (#8178) — <root>/<category>/<skill>/SKILL.md layout.
  • Plugin hot reload / clean unload (#7565, size/XXXL) — longer-horizon infrastructure work.
  • ESP32 hardware integration à la Meta Muse (#8189) — exploratory, unlikely in near-term release.

Prediction: the next minor/beta wave likely bundles Tavily/Firecrawl provider config, console basename configurability, and the Windows creator-plugin fixes; decision-model plumbing (#8205) suggests a subsequent release targeting agent routing.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain points: paid Tavily users cannot spend their own quota (#8174); binary assets are silently destroyed on GitHub skill install (#8179); Windows users cannot delete projects or even start Creator when a stale PID exists (#8206, #8194); tool approvals were functionally unusable until today's fix (#8105); LAN clients couldn't open the chat page (#8073).
  • Use cases observed: NAS/Docker self-hosting behind reverse proxies, multi-device chat (web + mobile, #8202), multi-agent worker containers running third-party coding CLIs (#8156), and external hardware integration (#8189).
  • Satisfaction signals: rapid turnaround — four fixes merged/closed and multiple same-day response PRs from first-time contributors. Users are engaging constructively (detailed repro steps, version/env metadata).
  • Dissatisfaction signals: recurring Windows desktop/creator reliability complaints, silent failures (empty completion, binary corruption, false-success cron), and desktop.log growth — a consistent "trust in the desktop build" theme.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  • #7016 — 工具调用 404 — Open since 2026-08-14 (~2 months), 4 comments, no linked fix PR. Streaming offload 404 loop is a core-path defect. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/7016
  • PR #6384 — AskUserQuestion interactive tool — Open since 2026-07-23 (~3 months) and "Under Review"; large user-facing capability stalled in review. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6384
  • PR #7565 — Plugin clean unload / rollback-safe hot reload — size/XXXL, open since 2026-09-04, touching plugin lifecycle; high architectural value, slow to land. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7565
  • PR #7964 — Langfuse tool observations never record output — Under Review since 2026-09-24; observability correctness for tool spans. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7964
  • Issue #8195 — Model pool has no delete/remove action — Small, clear UX gap; low effort, no fix PR yet. https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8195

Open-PR volume (20) is trending upward relative to merges (4), which — combined with multi-month "Under Review" items — suggests review bandwidth is the primary bottleneck rather than contribution supply.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-13

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remains in a high-activity, pre-release phase: 33 issues and 50 PRs were touched in the last 24h, yet 0 new releases shipped. The backlog skews heavily open — 29 of 33 active issues and 44 of 50 PRs are still open — indicating substantial incoming work relative to merge throughput. Activity is concentrated in four recurring themes: persistent memory, the A2A protocol, the plugin/WASM channel stack, and the ZeroCode TUI. Three issues closed on 2026-10-13 (a browser/search tool-semantics bug, plugin channel-instance seeding, and dead-worker settlement recovery), but the ratio of open-to-closed suggests reviewer/merge bandwidth, not contributor supply, is the current bottleneck. Notably, several of today's newest bug reports already have companion fix PRs opened the same day, which is a healthy sign for responsiveness.

2. Releases

No new releases in the reporting window. (Omit per instructions — no changelog, breaking changes, or migration notes to report.)

Two active release-gated trackers remain the roadmap anchors: #7432 Runtime and gateway delivery — v0.8.6 and v0.9.0 and the plugin-related work tagged release:v0.8.6 (#10999, PR #11262, PR #11261).

3. Project Progress

Closed/merged items (4 issues closed in the window; 3 visible):

Item Type Outcome
#11108 Bug (tools) Closed — map_tool_name_alias() no longer rewrites browser_open/browser/web_search into shell, preserving built-in tool semantics
#10996 Feature (plugins) Closed — channel-instance configuration/grants seeding during plugin install
#10331 Bug (runtime/daemon) Closed — recovery of terminal settlement intents abandoned by a dead worker
(4th closed issue) — Not in top-30 sample

PR activity (6 merged/closed; none visible in the top-20 sample, which is entirely OPEN): The visible PR set is dominated by fixes and follow-ups that advance existing epics rather than new subsystems. Standouts opened/first-seen today (2026-10-13):

  • PR #11698 — fix(runtime): snapshot personality files per session so edits no longer bust the prompt cache (addresses #11696).
  • PR #11693 — fix(tools): make model_routing_config upsert_agent preserve omitted fields and profile references (addresses #11606).
  • PR #11695 — fix(zerocode): align Cost-tab "By Period" totals to UTC (addresses #11694).
  • PR #11624 — fix(zerocode): answer dropped elicitations and record them (addresses #11623).
  • PR #11700 — fix(zerocode): keep composer/completion keystrokes out of the transcript.

Epic progress signals: The plugin stack by @IftekharUddin continues to mature (PR #11261, #11262, #11228), and ZeroCode UX/context work advances (PR #10905 manual context compaction, #11622 transcript timestamps).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume:

  1. #8692 — Maintainer decision queue for RFCs and design issues — 15 comments. The single most-discussed item. Underlying need: a transparent, prioritized decision pipeline for RFCs; the volume of design RFCs is outpacing maintainer decisions.
  2. #8891 — Persistent memory: wire curation/relevance/operability planes to parity — 11 comments. Tracks 7 open items (4 issues, 3 PRs). Need: cross-session memory parity with mature peer runtimes.
  3. #11254 — RFC: A2A protocol crate (zeroclaw-a2a) — 9 comments. Need: a first-class agent-to-agent wire model and discovery surface, building on #9106/#7763.
  4. #11420 — SQLite session backend rewrites created_at — 7 comments, priority:p1. High-engagement correctness bug.
  5. #7432 — Runtime & gateway delivery tracker (v0.8.6/v0.9.0) — 6 comments. Release-critical coordination.
  6. #11235 — RFC: Knowledge corpus (RAG) — 6 comments. Need: operator-owned document retrieval.
  7. #11074 — [[search_routes]] provider routing for web_search_tool — 5 comments. Need: per-query provider selection for source quality/corroboration.
  8. #10025 — RFC: zeroclaw swarm (ephemeral agent swarms + TUI) and #10573 — Bind pairing tokens to roster users — 4 comments each.

Analysis: Community demand clusters around multi-agent orchestration, durable memory/RAG, and identity-scoped access — i.e., users are pushing ZeroClaw from a single-assistant tool toward a coordinated, multi-tenant agent platform.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity/priority:

Severity Item Status Fix PR?
S1 – workflow blocked #11648 Web dashboard pairing input caps at 6 digits while backend issues 32-char alphanumeric codes OPEN Not indicated
p1 #11420 SQLite rewrites created_at for every message each turn (per-message times lost) OPEN Not indicated
p1 / high risk #11606 model_routing_config upsert_agent rewrites whole config, fabricates profiles, drops fields, resets limits OPEN, in-progress ✅ PR #11693
S2 #11655 Core conflict supersede hides unrelated memories when recall has no vector scores OPEN Not indicated
S2 (cost) #11696 System prompt rebuilt from disk every turn; personality edit busts cache for all live sessions OPEN ✅ PR #11698 + #11702
S2 #11623 ZeroCode drops pending ask_user/poll, leaving 600s timeouts and no record OPEN ✅ PR #11624
S3 #11658 Web chat input doesn't regain focus after reply OPEN Not indicated
S3 #11694 Cost tab mixes UTC and local-day totals without labeling OPEN ✅ PR #11695
S3 #11691 Paused-queue hint shows ⌥P, which types π in macOS Terminal OPEN Related PR #11700 (key handling)

Assessment: No crashes reported; issues are correctness/UX/cost regressions rather than hard failures. Positive signal: three of today's newest bugs already have same-day fix PRs, and one long-standing tool-semantics bug (#11108) closed. The p1 SQLite timestamp bug (#11420) is the most notable unaddressed stability item.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Most likely to land next (tied to v0.8.6/v0.9.0 trackers or already in PR):

  • Plugin system hardening/completion — channel-instance seeding (#10996, closed), Discord plugin proof (#10999), staged package replacement (PR #11261), plugin update CLI (PR #11262), TLS profile hardening (PR #11228).
  • Gateway separation / security — configurable MAX_BODY_SIZE (#11668), pairing-token-to-roster binding (#10573), scoped-principal log access (PR #11326).
  • ZeroCode UX — context compaction (PR #10905), transcript timestamps (PR #11622), draggable session rows (PR #11573).

Medium-term / RFC-stage (needs maintainer decision via #8692):

  • A2A protocol crate (#11254) — cross-cutting architecture RFC.
  • Knowledge corpus / RAG (#11235) — needs-author-action.
  • Ephemeral agent swarms (#10025) and Level 5 "Dark Factory" workflow (#11664) — strong user appetite for orchestration.
  • Separate Channels from Core (#11662) — reduce deadweight/attack surface.
  • Durable peer-agent turns (#9597), search_routes (#11074), turn-consolidation target category (#11657).

Prediction: The next release (v0.8.6) will most likely ship plugin-install/update hardening, gateway security scoping, and ZeroCode context/UX fixes. A2A, swarm, and RAG remain post-v0.9.0 architecture bets.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Multi-agent orchestration is the dominant unmet need. #11664 ("Level 5 Dark Factory Workflow"), #10025 (swarm TUI), and #11254 (A2A) all express the same pain: "standing up a team of agents requires config surgery… there is no orchestrator."
  • "Don't ship what I don't use." #11662 calls unused channels "deadweight and a security risk" — users want modular channel separation.
  • Multi-agent relay friction is real. #11668 reports long-context A2A message/send payloads being rejected by the gateway body limit in <1s with the opaque string length limit exceeded — a concrete production use case (front-desk → specialist agents).
  • Operator UX polish matters. Browser/search tools being silently rewritten to shell (#11108), pairing dialogs that break with 32-char codes (#11648), focus loss after replies (#11658), and mislabeled cost periods (#11694) show users are running ZeroClaw in real multi-agent setups and hitting ergonomic edges.
  • Satisfaction signal: fast same-day bug→fix turnaround on several items suggests an engaged maintainer group; dissatisfaction centers on review latency and unclear RFC decisions, not capability.

8. Backlog Watch

Items updated recently but long-open, needing maintainer attention (age = from creation to 2026-10-13):

Item Age Why it needs attention
#7432 Runtime & gateway delivery tracker (v0.8.6/v0.9.0) ~126 days Release-critical source of truth; still open
#8692 Maintainer decision queue ~101 days Most-commented item; RFC decision bottleneck
#8891 Persistent memory parity tracker ~96 days 7 open sub-items; high-severity dependency
#10025 zeroclaw swarm RFC ~58 days, needs-author-action Popular orchestration RFC awaiting input
#9597 Durable/attributable peer-agent turns ~74 days, in-progress Blocks reliable multi-agent lifecycle
#10290 Thread live config handle into detached turns ~50 days Security-relevant follow-up (SSRF policy propagation)
PR #10499 validate persistent config writes ~43 days, needs-author-action, size:XL High-risk config correctness
PR #10446 reject tool-call envelopes leaked into prose ~45 days, needs-maintainer-review Production-observed bug on gpt-5.6/codex
PR #10502 relocate tool-result images (OpenAI-compat 400) ~43 days, needs-author-action Blocks OpenAI-compatible providers
PR #10905 manual recoverable context compaction ~27 days, size:XL High-value ZeroCode feature stuck in review

Health read: The project has strong contributor momentum and a clear roadmap spine (memory → plugins → gateway separation → A2A/swarm). The primary risk is decision and review latency: three trackers with no-stale status and several needs-author-action/needs-maintainer-review PRs are accumulating. Clearing the maintainer decision queue (#8692) and unblocking the v0.8.6 plugin/gateway PR stack would most improve merge throughput.

Data notes: PR comment counts were not populated in the source sample (undefined), so PR ranking here reflects recency and state rather than comment volume. Only 3 of 4 closed issues and none of the 6 merged/closed PRs appear in the top-30/top-20 samples; details for the remainder are unavailable.

item.content:encoded:
AI 基础设施日报 2026-10-13

生成时间: 2026-10-13 03:08 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目对比报告 — AI 基础设施生态

摘要窗口：2026-10-13 · 项目：vLLM、SGLang、llama.cpp、Ollama、LiteLLM、Unsloth

计数说明：下文的“Issues”和“PRs”是*在 24 小时摘要中浮现的条目，并非仓库总数。它们包括开放的 bug、已关闭项、功能请求和路线图，因此请将其视为活跃度指标，而非缺陷计数。*

1. 生态概览

数据中心服务层（vLLM、SGLang、LiteLLM）今天发布了零个稳定版，而本地/边缘层则快速推进——llama.cpp 在一个窗口内落地了 11 个构建，Ollama 和 Unsloth 均推送了测试版。精力集中在少数前沿 MoE 架构（DeepSeek-V4/4.1、GLM-5.3-Flash、Qwen3.x、Gemma4），而最重要的在途工程是多适配器/MoE LoRA 服务（SGLang 的 21 部分运行时栈）以及预填充-解码分离作为默认的横向扩展拓扑。主要风险主题是推测解码，它同时是 vLLM、SGLang 和 llama.cpp 中被优化最多和最不稳定的特性。硬件广度持续扩大（AMD gfx942/gfx950/MI355X、Intel XPU/Arc、Ascend NPU、Apple MLX、Hexagon、AMX），但后端正确性错误——专家 ID 重复、FP8 加载缺口、MLX 内核恐慌——是反复出现的代价。

2. 活动对比

项目 层级 Issues（24小时） PRs（24小时） 发布状态
vLLM 数据中心服务引擎 ~21 ~14 无发布 — 最新发布列表为空
SGLang 数据中心服务引擎 ~27 ~20（包括 21 部分 LoRA 栈 #42880–#42888） 无发布
llama.cpp 本地/边缘 GGUF 运行时（ggml） ~19 ~23 11 个构建：b11567–b11577
Ollama 本地运行时 + 云产品 ~26 ~17 v0.40.4-rc0
LiteLLM LLM 网关 / 代理 ~24 ~14 无发布
Unsloth 微调 + Studio 运行时 ~29 ~15 v0.1.906-beta

解读表格： Ollama 和 Unsloth 的问题数量较多，反映的是活跃的缺陷/回归积压，而非新特性推进速度。llama.cpp 的当日问题与 PR 比率（~19:23）表明其修复吞吐量最健康；SGLang 正在分阶段落地最大的单一特性体（LoRA 运行时）。

3. 模型支持竞赛

项目 新落地架构 / 模型 显著缺口（请求或损坏）
vLLM Clef-Flash 通过 /v1/systemone 原生支持（Qwen3.5 骨干 + 联合模式头）；针对 DSv4 稀疏索引器的 DeepGEMM 26/09/30 升级；面向 SM120/SM121 路由专家的 NVFP4 每前向 W4A4/W4A16 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 在 SM8x 上无法运行（#50576）；GLM-5.3-Flash 在 sm_89 上无稀疏 MLA（#54059）；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 在 ROCm 上加载失败（#58688）；Gemma4 序列分类（#43726）；Qwen3.5-397B PD 分离（#43765）
SGLang GLM-5.3-Flash（共置预填充-注意力 CP + 解码/验证 TP，原生 MTP，DFlash2）；DeepSeek-V4.1 TP2 解码融合（融合全归约 + mHC 尾声，融合逆 RoPE + WO-A + MXFP8，SM100 交换 AB 注意力）；MiniCPM-V 4.7 指南；Marlin 上的 NVFP4 MoE LoRA；XPU 预填充图；NPU 预填充 CP AMD DSV4.1 稀疏解码因上游 aiter API 移除而损坏（#43765，关闭且无修复路径）
llama.cpp vLLM d3 / "pplx-decider"（b11572）和 d2（b11571），具有更严格的张量名称验证；当日多序列修复（b11577）；Hexagon Q1_0 HVX MUL_MAT；Intel Arc Pro B65；通过 NCCL 的多节点 TP；RPC supports_op 协商 在 --split-mode tensor 下失败的 MTP/DFlash2 草稿；Vulkan MUL_MAT_ID 行丢失（#29821）
Ollama llama.cpp b11521 → 决策模型 + EmbeddingGemma 2；CLI 决策模型支持；Prism 支持（PR 开放）；clef / clef flash 云；glm-ocr EOT 修复 Prism 三值 GGUFs（PQ2_0/PTQ1_0）导入失败（#18521）；请求 K2 Horizon 系列（#18698）
LiteLLM 无新模型/硬件集成；gpt-6 / Claude 5 桥接的成本对等测试；Gemini 上下文缓存创建令牌现已计费 Bedrock 自动发现请求关闭未修复（#43568）
Unsloth Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo（8 步图像生成）；来自预量化 DiT 的 LTX-2.5 fp8/int8；文本扩散 LLM 训练；更快的 MoE GGUFs；推测解码 Studio 中的 Ling 3.0（#8532）；Windows 上的 Gemma4e2b（#13388）；MLX 预训练结构（#8607）

谁领先：

  • SGLang 在前沿 MoE 部署深度上领先——它是唯一为 DeepSeek-V4.1 在 TP2 上交付生产解码融合以及完整 GLM-5.3-Flash 注意力拓扑的项目。
  • vLLM 拥有最广泛的模型和硬件矩阵，加上今天唯一原生新架构落地（Clef-Flash）以及前向 NVFP4 精度切换。
  • llama.cpp 在本地服务方面拥有最快的架构吸纳速度——在一个窗口内新增两个架构加上一个正确性修复。
  • Unsloth 拥有生成式多模态赛道（图像/视频），本集合中没有服务引擎原生覆盖。

4. 性能前沿

优化工作分散在六个不同的战场：

KV 缓存与前缀复用——最薄弱的一环，也是代理工作负载冲击最严重的地方。

  • vLLM：HIT_PENDING 没有截止时间，导致请求停滞直到客户端超时（#49829）；长预填充延迟模式（#61080）和自适应预填充预算 RFC（#52906）针对尾部延迟。
  • SGLang：EAGLE 推测解码 KV 索引重建现在针对 90k–170k KV-token 区间并行化（#42803）——明确是长上下文胜利。关键在于，两个代理式 KV 复用提案（#27574、#30928）均已停止活动，使得 RadixAttention 的字节完全相同前缀匹配成为唯一机制。
  • llama.cpp：新的 ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback（b11567）使推理中缓冲区重新预留可观测——真正的 p99 可诊断性升级。
  • Unsloth：每次工具调用后全上下文重新处理（#10698）——在约 30k token 时停滞数分钟。

量化/低精度——头条数字所在之处。

  • vLLM：NVFP4 MoE 每前向 W4A16→W4A4 切换（#54617）；但 FlashInfer NVFP4 因果预填充在 SM120 上比 FP8 慢 1.7–1.8 倍（#50416）。
  • SGLang：FP8 MoE LoRA Triton 供应商（#42885）、针对 B200、GB300、H200 调优的 CuTeDSL FP8 瓦片表（#42887）、在准备好的 Marlin 权重上的 NVFP4 MoE LoRA（#42888）。
  • llama.cpp：在 AMX Q4_K 解码上令牌生成 +13%，输出位完全相同（#30429）——今天最干净的可采用胜利；针对 gfx906/MI50 的 Q2_K VGPR 溢出修复（#29910）。
  • Unsloth：LTX-2.5 避免在加载时量化 38 GB bf16 transformer，降低峰值内存和启动成本。

内核/融合——丰富但狭窄。vLLM 的 mamba gather 融合（7 个 Triton 内核 → 1 个，约 6 倍）和 DFlash 填充（35.8 微秒/步）明确是孤立内核微基准，而非端到端吞吐量声明。SGLang 提出的 monokernel 框架（#43949，持久内核在 1–2 次启动中覆盖解码器层的大部分）是当前最雄心勃勃的结构性想法。

分布式/并行服务——SGLang 的 Q4 PD 分离路线图（#43699）将 PD 定位为主流部署形态；异构 TP KV 传输现在处理混合 SWA 模型（gpt-oss-120b，TP1 预填充 / TP4 解码，#40909）；预填充 CP 是 MHA/GQA 后端中最后一个未决项（#21788）。llama.cpp 增加了多节点 NCCL 张量并行（#28967）。

批处理与调度——vLLM run-batch 现在增量流式传输响应（前端内存，#52505）；SGLang 的 bench_serving --request-rate 逐渐偏离计划（#43930），这扭曲了基准基线。

推测解码——自成前沿，有真正的胜利（SGLang EAGLE 索引并行）和真正的危险（§6）。

5. 层级定位

层级 项目 角色与差异化因素
数据中心服务引擎 vLLM、SGLang GPU 优先、多 GPU/PD 感知、OpenAI 兼容 API。vLLM 在硬件/模型广度上竞争，并正在吸收网关关注点（可选 fastapi-guard 中间件，#60988）。SGLang 在前沿模型深度、长上下文/前缀密集型工作负载和 PD 分离上竞争，并进行最大的多适配器押注。两者现在都在交付以前属于网关层的功能（认证、速率限制、日志记录）。
本地/边缘运行时 llama.cpp、Ollama llama.cpp 是引擎 + ggml 后端层：GGUF、CPU/消费级 GPU/Apple/Hexagon、多后端。Ollama 是上层的产品化层——模型管理、CLI、桌面、云托管模型——并通过版本升级（b11521）显式跟踪 llama.cpp 上游。Ollama 现在通过云模型和工具调用向上扩展栈。
网关/代理 LiteLLM 不是推理引擎。拥有跨提供商协议转换、认证、预算、成本核算和 MCP 网关。其护城河是提供商覆盖广度和计费正确性——而非内核吞吐量。在边缘直接受到引擎原生中间件的威胁，但通过成本/可观测性/MCP 深度实现差异化。
训练/微调 + 本地应用运行时 Unsloth 微调、量化、GGUF 导出，以及 Studio 作为应用界面。独特地在一个栈中跨越 训练 → 量化 → 服务 → 代理，今天扩展到浏览器代理执行和图像/视频生成。将 llama.cpp 和 vLLM 作为后端嵌入，而非与之竞争。

边界模糊是故事主线： 引擎正在添加网关中间件，Ollama 正在添加云/代理功能，Unsloth 正在添加代理运行时，LiteLLM 正在添加 MCP 网关。集成表面——而非原始内核速度——是各层碰撞的地方。

6. 趋势信号

  1. DeepSeek-V4 / 前沿 MoE 是唯一的集成战场。 每个服务项目都在那里花费其最高信号的周期，而 AMD 始终是最后被支持的平台（SM8x 缺口、gfx950 稀疏解码中断、MI355X 追踪器）。
  2. 推测解码是生态系统中风险最高的生产特性。 四个运行时中有三个将其报告为最大不稳定源：SGLang 在任何 temperature > 0 时杀死服务器的 SIGKILL（#43412）、GLM-5.3 + DFLASH 静默质量崩溃（#40843）；llama.cpp 在量化目标上的分歧（#25618）和多 GPU 拆分上的 PP 减半（#27428）；Unsloth 的草稿路径；vLLM 的 DFlash/DSpark 在接受前缀缓存下的崩溃（#47930）。
  3. 多 LoRA / 多适配器服务是下一个解锁点——并且会引起动荡。 SGLang 的 21 部分栈（跨 Triton、CuTeDSL、Marlin 的 MoE LoRA，用于 FP8/NVFP4/BF16）是任何地方落地的最大特性。与此同时，vLLM 有一个未解决的 CUDA 图死锁，涉及融合 MoE LoRA + --fully-sharded-loras（#60845）。本季度计划评估，而非采用。
  4. 代理工作负载已经超越了引擎 KV 能力。 位置无关和程序化 KV 复用提案在 SGLang 中已死；引擎仍依赖字节完全相同的前缀匹配。今天的实际缓解措施是提示稳定性工程（固定前缀、有序工具模式）——加上对 llama.cpp 的 RAM 支持提示缓存在并发负载下可能跨对话泄露内容的认识（#27148），这对多租户服务器是一个数据隔离问题。
  5. 多租户和计费正确性现在是基础设施关注点。 LiteLLM 的 v1.93.0 Redis 故障破坏了缓存和预算计数器（#34614），v1.92 缺失 budget_fallbacks 列导致 Admin UI 阻塞（#33074），并且代理管理员 JWT 之前绕过了个人 max_budget（#41226）。Unsloth 修补了聊天工具工作区中的符号链接跟随以及 HF 令牌覆盖错误。
  6. 硬件多样化是真实的但脆弱的。 AMD gfx942/gfx950、Intel XPU/Arc B65、Ascend NPU 预填充 CP、Apple MLX、Hexagon HVX、Arm AMX 均有活动——然而 AMD DSV4.1 中断来自 SGLang 无法控制的上游 aiter API 移除，MLX SDPA 恐慌阻止了 Ollama 在 Apple Silicon 上运行。
  7. 发布节奏正在分化。 数据中心和网关层没有发布稳定版；本地/打包层发布了测试版和 11 个 llama.cpp 构建。固定并基准测试的纪律是强制性的：Ollama 据报告相比 v0.40.1 有 25–30% 吞吐量回归（#18968），而 LiteLLM 的公告使 v1.93.0/v1.92 成为不安全默认值。

作为代理/应用开发者应关注什么：

  • 在扩展代理循环之前测量每次工具调用的 TTFT——Unsloth 的重新处理回归（#10698）和普遍的 KV 复用缺口都在这里浮出水面。
  • 在您确切的安装方法上验证推测解码（pip 包 vs. 容器 vs. 源码），使用采样流量，并在量化目标上与非推测基线进行 diff。
  • 将内核级基准视为仅方向性参考——vLLM 的 6 倍 mamba 融合和 35.8 微秒 DFlash 节省是孤立测量；要求端到端数字。
  • 如果您运营长上下文或尾部延迟敏感型集群，请跟踪 SGLang 的 PD 分离路线图（#43699）和 vLLM 的长预填充延迟模式（#61080）。
  • 观察引擎原生中间件（vLLM 和 SGLang 中的 fastapi-guard）是否会侵蚀独立网关层——如果您正在标准化 LiteLLM 用于认证和速率限制而非成本/MCP/协议转换，则与此相关。

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 摘要 — 2026-10-13

来源：vllm-project/vllm

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新的 vLLM 版本发布。信号最强的活动围绕 DeepSeek-V4/DSv4.1：一个关于 SM8x/Ampere 支持的请求已有 109 条评论，一个 DSv4 CUDA-graph 压缩器修复，以及多份高并发稳定性报告。性能方面，一个 mamba align gather 融合声称在 kernel 层面带来 6 倍加速，同时新的 long-prefill defer 模式和可选的 API 安全中间件正在评审中。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

  • 没有新版本发布。 最新发布列表为空。
  • Mamba 配置弃用/清理： PR #60043 移除了 mamba_cache_mode="all" 的残留内容，并弃用 --mamba-cache-mode；Issue #60838 报告称，在该移除之后，--mamba-block-size 在有效配置中不再生效。应重新验证 Mamba/混合缓存调优。

4. 性能与优化

  • Mamba gather 融合： PR #58737 将 mamba align block-table gather 从 7 个 Triton kernel 融合为 1 个，在隔离 kernel 的所有 shape 上带来约 6 倍加速。范围说明：这是 kernel 级微基准测试，并非端到端吞吐量结论。
  • DFlash 推测解码 padding： PR #58633 并行化 DFlash draft-input padding，从单个 workgroup 节省最多 35.8 µs/step。同样是 kernel 级。
  • 长 prefill 延迟执行： PR #61080 添加了一种模式：如果超过阈值，每步有一个长 prefill 在等待请求之后、利用剩余预算运行。选择启用。
  • NVFP4 MoE 精度切换： PR #54617 在 SM120/SM121 上，对较小 token 数选择 W4A16，对较大 token 数选择 W4A4。
  • MoE router 融合： PR #57410 融合 Transformers 后端中在 top-k 之后打分的 MoE router。
  • 前端批处理流式输出： PR #52505 使 vllm run-batch 增量写入响应，而不是缓冲到结束，从而降低前端内存占用。
  • 已知性能缺口： Issue #50416 报告在 SM120 上 FlashInfer NVFP4 KV-cache causal prefill 比 FP8 慢约 1.7–1.8 倍；Issue #34635 报告 AllReduceFusionPass(config) 构造需要 1 秒以上；Issue #48229 报告每个 generate batch 会出现一次偶发的 0.7–2.0 秒 V1 engine step 冻结。
  • 活跃优化跟踪： Issue #57406 GLM-5.3，Issue #57149 和 Issue #59575 AMD MI355X，Issue #52906 自适应 prefill token 预算 RFC。

按严重程度排序：

  1. TP 挂起 / EngineDeadError — Issue #41530：DeepSeek-V4-Pro、TP=8、MTP 推测解码下出现 RPC sample_tokens 超时。仍开放；过去 24 小时数据中没有修复 PR。
  2. fused-MoE LoRA 下的 CUDA-graphs 死锁 — Issue #60845：vLLM 0.28.0、Qwen3.5 兼容的 35B-A3B MoE、TP=2/4、--fully-sharded-loras。仍开放；未注明修复 PR。

SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang 摘要 — 2026-10-13

今日亮点

DeepSeek V4 路线图已收官（#23602，75 条评论），W4A16 Hopper 支持与 Marlin 后续事项均已完成；与此同时，Q4 Prefill-Decode 分离路线图已发布（#43699），将 PD 定位为默认的横向扩展路径。当前规模最大的进行中工作是 21 部分的 LoRA runtime stack，正在向 Triton、CuTeDSL 和 Marlin 各 vendor 落地 MoE LoRA 支持（#42880–#42888）。风险方面，speculative decoding 在非 greedy 请求上可复现地导致服务器进程被杀死的崩溃（#43412）仍处于 open 状态。

发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内无新版本发布。值得注意的兼容性事项：

  • #43765 [CLOSED] — AMD DSV4.1 稀疏 decode 因外部依赖移除而损坏。 compact_attention_hip 导入了 aiter 的 pa_decode_sparse，而 aiter 已于 2026-09-18 移除该接口；升级 aiter 并不能 修复。影响近期 main 上的 gfx950 用户。
  • #30781 [CLOSED] — gateway/router 协议漂移。 sgl-model-gateway v0.3.2 拒绝了 type: "custom" 的 /v1/responses tools，破坏了 OpenAI Codex CLI 兼容性；根因是 Rust openai-protocol crate 落后于 Python protocol.py。
  • #33385 [CLOSED] — offload 行为未受 flag 门控。 Decode 模式 retract 因 NotImplementedError 崩溃，原因是 KV offload 无条件执行，而非由 --disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache 门控。
  • #43610 — 可选新依赖。 为没有 gateway 的部署新增 fastapi-guard 中间件（速率限制、IP 控制、载荷筛查）；状态是 per-worker 的，因此多 worker 场景推荐使用 Redis。
  • #42085 [OPEN] — 被静默忽略的配置。 --bf16-gemm-backend gemv 会被接受，但从未被未量化的线性层使用。

新模型与硬件支持

  • GLM-5.3-Flash — 同址部署的 prefill attention CP + decode/target-verify attention TP，原生支持 MTP 和 DFlash2（#43972，draft）。
  • DeepSeek-V4.1 — TP2 decode 路径现在可以使用此前仅限 TP4 的小批量 decode 融合（融合 all-reduce + mHC epilogues、融合 inverse-RoPE + WO-A + MXFP8、SM100 swap-AB decode attention）（#43838）。V4.1 优化另有跟踪：#42170。
  • MiniCPM-V 4.7 — 在模型支持合并前先添加了 cookbook（#43829）。
  • Marlin 上的 NVFP4 MoE LoRA — 基于已准备的 Marlin 权重的新 provider（#42888）。
  • XPU — 完整的 prefill graph 后端，实现与 decode 对等的 capture/replay（#30980）。
  • NPU — 面向通用（非 DSA）Ascend attention 后端的 prefill CP 修复，覆盖 Qwen3/Qwen3-MoE（#41564）；mamba checkpoint-pool 拷贝的 conv layout 对齐（#43845）；现已支持 prefill_complete（#43970）。
  • 异构 TP — PD KV 传输现在可以处理混合 SWA 模型（例如 gpt-oss-120b，prefill TP1 / decode TP4）（#40909）。

性能与优化

  • EAGLE spec-decode KV 索引构建已并行化，面向 flashinfer draft decode 和 verify/draft-extend（flashinfer、flashinfer_mla、aiter）按 token block 并行。目标是 90k–170k KV token 的长上下文场景，此前索引重建在每个请求内是串行的（#42803）。
  • 启动调优现在包含 FlashInfer 的默认 tactic（-1），避免选中对 profiling 输入而言比默认更慢的显式调优 tactic（#43927）。
  • LoRA runtime stack（第 13–21 部分） — 带 FP8 行量化和 masked/contiguous 行域的 MoE LoRA stage kernels（#42880）；面向 SM90（WGMMA）和 SM100（tcgen05）的 CuTeDSL BF16 grouped GEMM（#42884）；packed MoE schedules（#42883）；FP8 MoE LoRA Triton vendor（#42885）；为 B200、GB300 和 H200 调优的 CuTeDSL FP8 tile tables（#42887）。
  • 进行中的路线图： 剩余 MHA/GQA 后端（flashinfer/trtllm-mha）的 Prefill Context Parallelism 是 #21788 中最后一个未完成事项；diffusion Q4 以 MiniMax-H3 为目标，包含通信/计算重叠以及已验证的 GB200/GB300 配方（#43313）；block-diffusion（dLLM）服务路线图在 #39499 中继续推进。
  • 提议： 一个 monokernel 框架（persistent kernels，在一次或两次 launch 中覆盖一个 decoder 层的大部分），包含按模型划分的规格和 CI 门禁（#43949）。

稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. #43412 [OPEN] — spec decoding 在首个 sampled 请求上 SIGKILL 服务器进程树。 Greedy（temp 0）可用；任何 temperature > 0 都会挂掉。触发原因是当 pip 安装包自带的 cccl 与 pip cu13 toolkit 冲突时，flashinfer verify-sampling JIT 失败。未引用修复 PR——在仅 pip 安装且有 sampled 流量的环境中避免启用 speculative decoding。
  2. #43557 [OPEN] — PD runtime 角色切换因非法内存访问而崩溃，发生在 decode → prefill → decode 之后，环境为 sglang 0.5.21、mooncake 后端、TP1、--enable-pd-role-switch（Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B）。
  3. #40843 [OPEN] — GLM-5.3 + DFLASH spec decoding 产生严重重复和退化循环，即正确性失败，而不仅仅是崩溃。
  4. #43526 [OPEN] — gfx942 block-FP8 linear AITER CK blockscale GEMM 的精度问题（AMD）。
  5. #43765 [CLOSED] — gfx950 上的 DSV4.1 稀疏 decode 因 ModuleNotFoundError 失败，原因是上游 aiter API 移除。
  6. #42085 [OPEN] — GEMV BF16 GEMM 后端 flag 静默 no-op，因此用户可能基准测试的是一条实际从未走到的路径。
  7. #43709 [OPEN] — transcription multipart upload 没有应用层大小限制（在接受上传的端点上存在资源耗尽暴露面）。
  8. #43930 [OPEN] — bench_serving --request-rate 逐渐落后于计划，因此实际达到的请求速率低于请求速率，并使基准测试结果产生偏差。
  9. #42752 [OPEN] — CI flaky-test / 基础设施跟踪帖（49 条评论），监控 NVIDIA PR Test Base 和 PR Test Extra；补充了更早的 CI 跟踪帖 #17050。预计 CI 门控 PR 的审查延迟会升高。
  10. 因不活跃而关闭的正确性/健壮性 bug 在更新窗口内重新浮现：#29998（runai_streamer 在 TP8 下静默损坏 GLM-5.2）、#34384（DSpark ragged CUDA Graph geometry）、#34399（paged KV allocator 在 OOM 检查之前就启动 kernels）、#26618（radix-cache prefix 命中后 FlashInfer MIS delimiter indices）、#31019（GPT-OSS Harmony 在 require_reasoning + json_schema 下输出格式错误）、#31766（prefill 侧 fd 耗尽）。

对应用开发者的意义

  • 多租户 / 多适配器服务是即将到来的重大解锁。 21 部分的 LoRA stack 覆盖面向前沿服务形态（FP8、NVFP4、BF16）的 MoE LoRA，并为 Hopper/Blackwell 提供厂商特定 GEMM。如果你为每个基础模型服务大量 fine-tune，计划在该 stack 合并后评估——但这是一次大型、分阶段落地，预计会有变动。
  • 面向 agent 的 KV 复用仍未在引擎层面解决。 两个 agent 导向的提案——Programmatic KV Cache（#27574，现已关闭）和 Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse（#30928，已关闭）——都转为不活跃。具有共享 system prompts、tool schemas 以及不同偏移检索文档的 Agent/RAG 工作负载，仍依赖 RadixAttention 的字节级相同前缀匹配；请自行做 prompt 稳定性工程（固定前缀、有序 tool schemas）以最大化缓存命中。
  • 目前在生产环境中对 speculative decoding 要保守。 在 sampled 流量下它可能拖垮整个服务器（#43412），而在 GLM-5.3 + DFLASH 下它会静默降低输出质量（#40843）。启用前请在你确切的安装方式（pip bundle vs. container）上验证。
  • 如果你运行带角色切换的 PD disaggregation，请固定到已知良好版本，并演练 decode → prefill → decode 转换（#43557）。Q4 路线图（#43699）表明该拓扑现已成为主流部署形态，因此修复应该会很快落地。
  • 依赖非标准 OpenAI tool 类型的 gateway 用户应确保其 router 使用已同步 protocol crate 的构建（#30781）；否则 Codex-CLI 风格客户端将收到请求拒绝。
  • 硬件覆盖持续扩大——NPU prefill CP、XPU prefill graphs 和 AMD gfx942/gfx950 今天都有活动，但 AMD 稀疏 decode 路径存在 SGLang 无法控制的外部依赖风险（#43765）。
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-10-13

1. Today's Highlights

A rapid-fire release window (b11567–b11577) landed new model support for the vLLM "d2" and "d3" architectures plus a follow-up multi-sequence correctness fix, alongside a graph-level fix padding no-cache attention KV to 256 for head size 512 on CUDA. Backend correctness was the dominant theme: Metal's mul_mat_id was fixed for duplicate expert IDs, while Vulkan's equivalent bug (#29821) remains open. Performance work continues on several fronts, with a reported +13% token generation on AMX CPUs for Q4_K decode.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • b11567 — new scheduling API: ggml_backend_sched_realloc_callback / ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback lets applications observe when graph buffers are re-reserved mid-inference. Additive, but the first step toward surfacing reallocation-driven latency spikes. (PR #30329)
  • b11570 — build system change: llama_build() / llama_build_and_test() now accept a LINK keyword (default llama-common); ggml-only tests link only ggml. Downstream CMake consumers that relied on implicit llama-common linkage for their own test targets should audit their call sites. (PR #30299)
  • CI/release packaging: OpenVINO release binaries now build with GGML_NATIVE=OFF, GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON, and GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON, fixing AVX-512 STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION crashes on non-AVX-512 hosts. Broken OpenVINO download links in release notes were also repaired. (PR #30324, PR #30401)

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • vLLM d3 / "pplx-decider" models (b11572, PR #30383) and d2 (b11571, PR #30378) — new architecture support with stricter tensor-name validation and documented naming rules; b11577 fixes a non-causal + hybrid + multi-sequence graph case (PR #30408).
  • Hexagon Q1_0 — native HVX MUL_MAT for Q1_0, direct {-1,+1} expansion against tiled Q8_0 activations, plus 2D/4D/matvec workers (PR #30122).
  • Intel Arc Pro B65 (Vulkan) — shader core count added; the device reports as BMG G31, same die as B70 with cores disabled (PR #30431).
  • Multi-node tensor parallelism via NCCL — new backend collective interface implemented in CUDA and wired into the RPC server; stacked on prior multi-GPU work (PR #28967).
  • Hexagon HTP power profiles — GGML_HEXAGON_POWER_MODE selects one of eight DCVS/HMX profiles, with burst preserved as default (PR #30423).
  • RPC capability negotiation — RPC client now queries the remote backend's supports_op instead of assuming universal op support (PR #28571).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • AMX Q4_K decode: +13% tg — M=1 VNNI kernel now walks each Q4_K group across output columns and broadcasts Q8 activation dwords directly, rather than column-by-column. Numerically identical output order (PR #30429).
  • Vulkan f16 accumulation packing — packed FMA path for f16 accumulation without a dot-product op; dot_product variant packs two rows per f16 FMA and was renamed to dot_product_v2 (b11573, PR #29877).
  • Vulkan RMS norm — workgroup reduction replaced with two-stage subgroup reductions; benchmarked on B70 Arc Pro, RTX 4060 Ti, and 7900 XT (PR #29882).
  • Hexagon CPY/CONCAT round 3 — converting copies moved into per-DMA-descriptor row blocks so short rows are no longer DMA-latency bound; adds a threaded DMA/HVX gather-row helper (b11574, PR #30341).
  • Q2_K VGPR spill fix (CUDA/AMD) — softer unroll and removal of an unnecessary temporary loop to eliminate heavy mmq register spilling on gfx906/MI50 (PR #29910).
  • Logits buffer allocation skipped when the graph produces no logits — saves ~1 MiB host RAM per output for large-vocab embedding/reranking models (bge-m3: 250002, EmbeddingGemma: 262144) (PR #30255).
  • No-cache attention graph fix (b11576): KV dimension padded to 256 so FLASH_ATTN_EXT on CUDA satisfies the multiple-of-FATTN_KQ_STRIDE requirement for head size 512 (PR #30416).

5. Stability & Regressions

High severity

  • Server RAM-backed prompt cache cross-conversation leakage — server_prompt_cache (--cache-ram, default enabled) can restore content from an unrelated finished conversation into a fresh slot under concurrent load. This is a correctness and data-isolation issue for multi-tenant servers. No fix PR yet. (Issue #27148)
  • CUDA graphs hang GPU channel (RC watchdog + Xid 8) on RTX 5090 Laptop / sm_120; GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is a complete workaround. (Issue #27330)

Correctness

  • Speculative decoding divergence on quantized targets — greedy (temp=0, top_k=1) draft-mtp/draft-dspark can diverge from vanilla output with Q4_K_M targets while bf16 targets match. (Issue #25618)
  • Vulkan MUL_MAT_ID row loss — duplicate expert IDs in a token's row produce partial/dropped output when n > 8, due to group-counting mismatch between slot counting and count_experts. Open. (Issue #29821)
  • Metal mul_mat_id duplicate IDs — same class of bug; fixed in b11569, which also corrected kernel naming and the previous one-match-per-token / ne21-capacity assumption. (PR #30373)
  • Nondeterministic FA prefill with Qwen 3.5 9B on RDNA3 (ROCm/HIP) for multimodal requests since b10905. (Issue #30175)
  • DFlash2 / MTP draft failures with tensor split — assertion failures and FA head-dim mismatches across CUDA/SYCL/Vulkan when combining speculative decoding with --split-mode tensor. Multiple reports; largely unresolved. (Issue #27819, Issue #24440, Issue #29418, Issue #29419)
  • Server batch_view offset not propagated to ctx_dft — subtler batch-retry path in update_slots() can mis-address the draft context. (Issue #24840)

Performance regressions / backend stability

  • draft-mtp halves prompt processing on multi-GPU layer split (single GPU unaffected). (Issue #27428)
  • Glimmer: memory growth + prefill slowdown after first mmproj use. (Issue #26873)
  • Vulkan ErrorDeviceLost on 7900 XTX during decode. (Issue #30010)
  • OpenVINO: Cannot get length of dynamic dimension when -fa off (V cache transposed past FA-layout assumptions) — fix PR open (PR #30350); separate i5-1345u exception still open (Issue #27546).
  • HIP gfx1151 (Strix Halo, Windows): SOLVE_TRI aborts with rocBLAS hipErrorInvalidImage, affecting unfused gated-delta-net paths (Qwen3.5 / Kimi-linear). (Issue #27557)
  • ggml-rpc SIGABRT on unreachable endpoint — startup failures now fail gracefully rather than killing the process (PR #30415); SYCL get_rows on reordered quantized weights fixed (PR #30430).

Resolved/closed

  • KV cache save via /slots/N?action=save for vision models (#19466); Qwen3-Coder tool-call parser (#15012); Metal tensor API silently inert on M5+/A19+ due to unset MTLCompileOptions.languageVersion (#27473); Vulkan Q8_0 PP regression after #25773 (#30000).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • New model coverage is expanding fast but sequence-handling edge cases lag. The vLLM d2/d3 additions landed with a same-day multi-sequence fix (b11577). If you serve these models, validate non-causal + hybrid attention configurations with batched, multi-slot requests before production.
  • Multi-tenant server deployments need attention. The prompt-cache leak (#27148) is the most consequential open item for anyone running llama-server with --cache-ram defaults under concurrency — it can surface content from an unrelated conversation. Consider disabling cross-slot caching until patched.
  • Speculative decoding remains the least stable surface. Divergence on quantized targets, PP halving on multi-GPU splits, and tensor-split crashes with MTP drafts all remain open. Avoid combining --split-mode tensor with draft/MTP speculation on quantized targets in production, and validate greedy outputs against a non-speculative baseline.
  • Duplicate-expert-ID handling is a recurring backend bug class. Metal is fixed; Vulkan is not. MoE workloads with skewed router distributions should pin to a build ≥ b11569 on Metal, and treat Vulkan MoE output as suspect until #29821 closes.
  • Observability for latency spikes improves. The new ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback (b11567) lets you detect when KV/graph buffers are re-reserved mid-inference — useful for correlating p99 latency jumps with memory pressure rather than attributing them to the model.
  • CPU throughput on AMX servers improves measurably. The Q4_K decode path (+13% tg) is worth adopting for CPU-only or CPU-offload decode tiers, with bit-identical outputs easing rollout.
  • Aligned build flags matter for shipped binaries. The OpenVINO AVX-512 crash reinforces checking GGML_NATIVE=OFF in any distribution pipeline — the same class of failure applies to self-built binaries moved between hosts.
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama 摘要 — 2026-10-13

1. 今日亮点

Ollama 发布了 v0.40.4-rc0，将 llama.cpp 更新至 b11521，以支持决策模型和 EmbeddingGemma 2，并在推理路由中复用已验证的 manifests/已加载模型（PR #18917、PR #18947）。最严重的活跃信号是据报告所有模型相较 v0.40.1 出现 25–30% 吞吐量回归（Issue #18968），以及 0.40.x 中 Apple Silicon 上多起 MLX SDPA 内核 panic（Issue #18966、Issue #18940）。工具支持工作仍在继续：一个开放 PR 将允许在结构化输出中使用工具调用，解决当前 format: json 工具调用损坏的问题（Issue #18944、PR #18975）。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

  • v0.40.4-rc0 — 面向 v0.40.4 的 RC。包含用于决策模型和 EmbeddingGemma 2 的 llama.cpp b11521，以及服务器在推理路由中复用已验证的 manifests 和已加载模型（发布、PR #18917、PR #18947）。发布说明被截断；MLX 变更无法完全看到。
  • 提供的数据中未明确指出破坏性 API/配置变更。从运维角度，注意当请求 shift 与已加载 runner 不同时调度器的重载行为（Issue #18950）。
  • 文档清理：在 PR #18970 中移除了过时的 OLLAMA_TMPDIR 和 %TEMP% 引用；在 PR #18960 中回退了文档重构。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • 决策模型 + EmbeddingGemma 2：llama.cpp 升级至 b11521；在 PR #18962 中添加了 CLI 决策模型支持；在 PR #18974 中修复了 MLX 决策模型 JSON 状态提示。
  • Prism 模型：开放 PR 添加 Prism 模型支持（PR #18967）；Prism 三进制 GGUF（PQ2_0/PTQ1_0）仍是一个存在导入失败的跟踪 issue（Issue #18521）。
  • K2 Horizon 系列：关于 k2-horizon 架构的功能请求，规模为 0.9B–36B MoE（Issue #18698）。
  • 云模型：PR 在云上引入 clef 和 clef flash（PR #18969）。
  • 旧版 glm-ocr GGUF：PR 将 <|user|> 注册为 EOT，以防止输出失控（PR #17195）。
  • Windows 模型存储：PR 通过 Windows junction/卷挂载点查找模型，修复在 NTFS 挂载路径上使用 OLLAMA_MODELS 时 ollama list 为空的问题（PR #18949、Issue #18921）。
  • 后端/硬件问题：RTX 5090 搭配 Cohere MoE 出现 CUDA 非法内存访问（Issue #18642）；AMD RX 6800 XT 上出现 Vulkan 访问冲突（Issue #18557）；Windows CUDA 后端 .dll 被保留为 .tmp，导致 CPU 回退（Issue #18712）；Apple Silicon 上出现 MLX SDPA panic（Issue #18966、Issue #18940）。

4. 性能与优化

  • 据报告，所有模型相较 v0.40.1 出现 25–30% 吞吐量回归，tokens/sec 更低（Issue #18968）。暂无修复 PR。
  • 提示计时指标修复：开放 PR 按已评估的 token 计算提示计时，修复热提示缓存下 prompt_per_second 虚高的问题（PR #18964、Issue #18948）。
  • KV/VRAM 核算：开放 PR 在 PredictServerVRAM 中镜像 GraphSize KV 核算，目标是解决 Qwen 加载/内存预测问题（PR #17615）。
  • 调度器重载行为：提议启动支持 shift 的 runner，并按请求强制 shift:false，避免在 resolveContextShift 不同时发生重载（Issue #18950）。
  • MLX 内存泄漏：已关闭 issue 报告使用 qwen3.6:27b-mlx 时，每次工具调用请求在前缀缓存预算之外泄漏约 0.43 GiB（Issue #18620）。
  • KV 缓存预热：功能请求：对系统提示 KV 缓存进行预热，以降低大型系统/工具提示下的首次响应延迟（Issue #18952）。
  • 推理路由复用：v0.40.4-rc0 在推理路由中复用已验证的 manifests 和已加载模型（PR #18947）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. Apple Silicon 上的 MLX SDPA 内核 panic（0.40.x） — 在 M2 Max、M6 等设备上，搭配 Qwen 3.8、Gemma 4、qwen3.6:35b-mlx 和 gemma4:e2b-mlx 时出现“Maximum threads per threadgroup is 896 but requested 1024/960”。多个重复项：Issue #18846 已关闭，Issue #18856 已关闭，Issue #18940 已关闭，Issue #18966 开放，Issue #18885 开放。相关多模态嵌入在小 num_ctx 下的 500 已由 PR #18973 修复。
  2. 25–30% 性能回归：所有模型相较 v0.40.1 出现 25–30% 性能回归（Issue #18968）。
  3. 使用 format: json 时工具调用损坏 — 设置 JSON 格式后模型无法使用工具调用（Issue #18944）。开放 PR PR #18975 将允许在结构化输出中使用工具调用。
  4. 在 Windows 上，RTX 5090 搭配 Cohere MoE 架构出现 CUDA 非法内存访问（Issue #18642）。
  5. AMD RX 6800 XT 上 Vulkan 崩溃 — 加载任何模型时发生访问冲突（Issue #18557）。
  6. Windows CUDA 后端自动更新失败 — ggml-cuda.dll 被保留为 .tmp，VRAM 为 0 B / 回退到 CPU（Issue #18712）。
  7. shift 不匹配时调度器重载模型 — 可能导致延迟/吞吐量波动（Issue #18950）。
  8. Windows 上使用 NTFS 挂载点时 ollama list 为空 — 修复 PR 已开放（Issue #18921、PR #18949）。
  9. Qwen3-Coder 工具解析器损坏 int64 范围外的数字 — 例如 1e20 变成 9223372036854775807（Issue #18421）。
  10. 云回归：云模型忽略 JSON 回复 schema（Issue #12362）；deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud 在图像输入超过约 655,360 tokens 时返回 500（Issue #18853）。
  11. 其他平台 bug：在 Raspberry Pi/Debian 13 上第二次 ollama run 卡住（Issue #18796）；Windows GPU 发现控制台闪烁（Issue #18954）；Windows 托盘服务器始终无法启动（Issue #18507 已关闭）；Windows Defender 误报（Issue #2519 已关闭）；manifests-v2 出现奇怪别名（Issue #18870 已关闭）；gpt-oss 出现 ffn_down_exps.weight size overflows（Issue #18869 已关闭）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 升级到 0.40.x 前先固定版本/做基准测试：25–30% 的回归和 MLX panic 使 v0.40.4-rc0 对生产 Apple Silicon 和延迟敏感型部署存在风险。如果使用 MLX，考虑留在 0.35.x，直到 SDPA panic 被修复。
  • 结构化输出 + 工具：如果你将 format: json 与工具调用一起使用，目前预计会出问题；关注 PR #18975。请校验工具调用参数的数值精度，尤其是使用 Qwen3-Coder 时（Issue #18421）。
  • 云输出：对某些云模型而言，JSON schema 强制执行不可靠；应在服务端进行校验，而不是信任 schema（Issue #12362）。
  • Windows 模型存储：如果 OLLAMA_MODELS 位于 junction/挂载点上，在 PR #18949 合入前，ollama list 可能为空。
  • 指标：PR #18964 中的提示计时修复将改变热缓存下的 prompt_per_second；请相应调整仪表盘。
  • Agent 延迟：对于长上下文 agent 工作负载，跟踪系统提示 KV 缓存预热请求（Issue #18952）和调度器 shift 重载修复（Issue #18950）。
  • 值得关注的解析器修复：Cohere 块排序（PR #18965）、FunctionGemma 调用间内容（PR #18961）、Gemma4 空白字符（PR #17570）和 glm-ocr EOT（PR #17195）——如果你的 agent 依赖这些模型系列，则这些修复相关。

版本发布与破坏性变更

  • 无新版本发布。
  • v1.93.0 回归： Redis 缓存失败，报错 TypeError: AbstractConnection.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ssl_check_hostname'。导致缓存和预算计数器失效。Issue #34614
  • v1.92 回归： 缺少 budget_fallbacks 列导致致命问题（无法登录 Admin UI 等）。Issue #33074
  • OpenTelemetry SDK 锁定在 1.28.0，阻碍升级；有人请求迁移到 1.40 系列或放宽版本范围。Issue #29407

新模型与硬件支持

  • 本时间窗口内没有新模型或硬件支持公告。（Bedrock 自动发现功能请求已关闭：Issue #43568）

性能与优化

  • Prometheus 多进程目录隔离： 每次代理启动现在都会获得自己自动创建的 PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR，防止一个代理清除另一个代理的实时计数器。PR #42660
  • MCP 网关进度/取消： 进度消息通过发起请求的 SDK 通道转发；HTTP 取消现在会及时取消上游工作。PR #46134
  • 透传端点 CPU 修复： 导致 100% CPU 的无界注册表增长问题已关闭。Issue #26081
  • 未报告具体的吞吐量/延迟数据。

稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. Redis 缓存失败（v1.93.0） — 导致缓存和预算计数器失效。仍开放。Issue #34614
  2. budget_fallbacks 列缺失（v1.92） — Admin UI 致命问题。仍开放。Issue #33074
  3. 代理管理员 JWT 绕过个人 max_budget — 安全/计费绕过。已关闭。Issue #41226
  4. 流式 500：NoneType + int，当后端 chunk 省略 choices[].index 时发生。仍开放。Issue #46047
  5. websearch_interception 泄漏 max_parallel_requests 槽位，每次使用 web_search 工具流式调用 /v1/messages 时发生。仍开放。Issue #46093
  6. 100-599 之外的 SSE 错误码被丢弃 — 路由器回退/冷却永远不会触发。仍开放。Issue #31284
  7. 部署自定义定价被忽略：在 model-cost-map 重新加载后（input_cost_per_token: 0）。仍开放。Issue #30081
  8. Bedrock 音频转写 HTTP 400，原因是系统消息与音频块不兼容。仍开放。Issue #41544
  9. A2AConfig 静默丢弃 temperature/max_tokens/top_p。仍开放。Issue #45944
  10. Key 过期时间戳被忽略 — 持久化的过期时间改为从时长推导。仍开放。Issue #45236
  11. 非管理员用户无法通过 UI 为个人 key 设置 max_budget。 仍开放。Issue #33212
  12. Master key 认证错误缺少客户端 IP。 仍开放。Issue #33150
  13. 模型别名权限在别名解析前被拒绝。 仍开放。Issue #25281
  14. Codex CLI Responses API 工具调用状态未正确关闭。 仍开放。Issue #30603
  15. 不稳定的 MCP schema 校验测试（约 25% 失败）。仍开放。Issue #46071

今日修复/关闭：

  • 移除了 Gemini 3 temperature 注入（Issue #38663、Issue #45333）
  • Gemini 工具使用提示 token 现会计费（Issue #45991）
  • MCP 二进制资源现在正确返回（Issue #32330）
  • MCP OAuth 401 + RFC 9728 元数据（Issue #31296）
  • 透传端点 CPU（Issue #26081）
  • Minimax 编码计划 API 认证（Issue #24483）

这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 谨慎升级： v1.93.0 的 Redis bug 和 v1.92 的 budget_fallbacks 问题可能破坏缓存和 Admin UI。部署前请测试。
  • 计费准确性： 如果你使用 Gemini 上下文缓存或 Azure Claude 网络搜索，请确保所用构建包含最新计费修复；此前存在少计费/多计费问题。
  • MCP 用户： 网关现在会转发进度并及时取消上游工作 — 带来更好的用户体验和资源利用率。
  • Anthropic /v1/messages： 503 响应现在映射为 529 overloaded_error，与 Anthropic 的契约保持一致，并改进 Claude Code 的重试行为。
  • 可观测性： 被追踪响应上的 W3C traceresponse 头（PR #42079）有助于将网关请求与 trace 关联。
  • 成本跟踪： 批量 JSONL 行项目可以存储在回调中（PR #41691），用于逐请求成本对账。
  • 护栏： 新增 Wingback 护栏集成（PR #46136）。
  • 关注未解决的 bug： Key 过期时间戳、非管理员 max_budget UI、模型别名权限以及流式 choices[].index 问题可能影响生产环境；请跟进关联 issue 以获取修复。
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth 摘要 — 2026-10-13

来源：github.com/unslothai/unsloth

1. 今日亮点

v0.1.906-beta 带来两项核心能力：智能体式 Browser Use（模型可以打开、阅读、点击、输入和滚动页面）以及 Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo（8 步图像生成），此外还有文本扩散 LLM 训练、更快的 MoE GGUF 和投机解码。与此同时，浏览器智能体获得了底层控制能力——坐标点击、鼠标移动、拖拽以及经批准的脚本执行 (PR #13505) ——并且 LTX-2.5 fp8/int8 现在加载预量化的 DiT，而不是在加载时量化 38 GB bf16 transformer (PR #13516)。影响最大的未解决回归仍然是 Studio 中每次工具调用后重复完整上下文再处理 (Issue #10698)。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

  • v0.1.906-beta — Browser Use + Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo。还附带文本扩散 LLM 训练、更快的 MoE GGUF 和投机解码（源中发布说明被截断）。无需迁移步骤。
  • Studio CLI: --models-dir PATH（可重复）已添加到 unsloth studio，用于指向本地模型文件夹；通过 PR #13435 合入，关闭 Issue #8250。
  • 凭据行为变更： 将 token= 传给 FastLanguageModel/FastModel.from_pretrained 此前会覆盖 hf auth login 会话。该问题已在 PR #13486 修复——此前为受限模型传入的只读 token 可能悄无声息地破坏后续 push。
  • Docker： UNSLOTH_STUDIO_KEEP_LEGACY=0 现在会通过 docker/run.sh 传播 (PR #13488)。
  • API 缺口（仍未解决）： Model List API 未暴露按量化方案选择的能力，因此无法以编程方式选择 Q8 还是 Q4_K_M——Issue #9340。
  • 测试/CI 相关： Studio 启动器现在支持由 Kaggle 支持的 notebook 配合 Cloudflare quick tunnel (PR #6987)。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo — 8 步图像生成；随 v0.1.906-beta 发布。一个相关分类 bug（general.architecture=qwen_image21 的扩散 GGUF 被归为文本生成并从 Images 页面隐藏，AMD ROCm）已关闭：Issue #13328。
  • LTX-2.5 fp8/int8 — 现在从托管的预量化 DiT（unsloth/LTX-2.5-FP8）初始化加载，而不是在运行时量化 (PR #13516)；VAE fixture、catalog 行和 Video 页面默认值见 PR #13500。
  • 文本扩散 LLM 训练和更快的 MoE GGUF 支持随 v0.1.906-beta 发布。
  • 非 CUDA 加速器： vLLM resume/teardown 现在通过当前激活的加速器（NPU/XPU）释放设备缓存，而不是在非 CUDA 环境下静默 no-op——PR #13438。
  • 本地模型提供方： On-Device 检测现在覆盖 LM Studio、Ollama、自定义文件夹、./models、Hermes 和 oMLX，并支持可用的 reveal/delete——PR #13507。Audio.cpp 伞形仓库模型（audio-cpp/audio.cpp-gguf）现在可按文件夹列出/显示/删除——PR #13519。
  • 已请求、尚未支持： Studio 中的 Ling 3.0（Issue #8532，👍5）；Windows 上的 Gemma4e2b（Issue #13388）；使用独立 llama.cpp 配置的多个并发服务器（Issue #8488，已关闭）；使用自定义 .crt/.key SSL 而不是仅 Cloudflare HTTPS（Issue #8716）；MLX 预训练/语料打包结构（Issue #8607）。

4. 性能与优化

  • 投机解码和 更快的 MoE GGUF 路径随 v0.1.906-beta 发布（发布说明被截断；未发布基准测试）。
  • Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo 的 8 步图像生成——显著减少扩散服务的步数。
  • LTX-2.5 加载时间： 避免在加载时量化 38 GB bf16 transformer，降低峰值内存和启动开销 (PR #13516)。
  • 回归——上下文再处理： 每次工具调用后似乎都会重新处理完整上下文；在约 30k token 时，这意味着每次工具调用要等待数分钟，归因于此前某次 Studio 更新引入的变更——Issue #10698。尚无关联修复 PR。
  • 回归——CPU 饱和： token 生成期间出现 100% CPU 峰值，自 Issue #6046 以来一直存在。
  • ROCm 上未遵循 VRAM/RAM offload： 在 AMD ROCm 上，即使勾选“No RAM Offload”，模型仍会从 VRAM 卸载并停放到 RAM——Issue #10341。
  • UI 卡顿： 大代码块会导致界面卡顿（Issue #10769）；Library 卡片悬停/选中对比度和 time-pill 居中已调整（PR #13509，#13518）。

5. 稳定性与回归问题

按严重程度排序；已注明修复状态。

  1. 工具调用上下文再处理（性能回归，无修复） — 长上下文下每次工具调用停顿数分钟。Issue #10698
  2. 大型 MoE 长上下文 OOM — Qwen2.5 72B 4-bit 在 A800 上 32k 时 OOM，而 24k 稳定；这与 Llama 3.3 70B 已发布 80k+ 的说法相矛盾。Issue #2937
  3. 桌面端拖放损坏 — 拖放文件时静默未附加，不显示错误。Issue #13473
  4. Wayland/GNOME/Arch 上桌面 AppImage 窗口尺寸不可用 — 无法调整大小、帧率问题、多显示器。Issue #12845
  5. 聊天客户端崩溃 — tapClientLookup: Index 1 out of bounds、消息部分格式错误、“New chat”时重复 toolCallId。Issue #10288
  6. 训练期间 UNSLOTH_RETURN_LOGITS=1 被静默重置为 0 — 破坏 Gemma 3 上的自定义验证指标。标记为已修复，待确认。Issue #3071
  7. Blackwell（RTX 5090）启动失败 — PY_SSIZE_T_CLEAN macro must be defined；已关闭。Issue #2760
  8. Qwen3 几分钟后 deallocating None — 梯度检查点与内存管理冲突；已关闭。Issue #2955
  9. 本地 RTX 5060 Ti 上 vLLM 后端加载失败（vllm_process failed to load!）；已关闭。Issue #2963
  10. 模型加载失败 — unsloth/GLM-OCR（Issue #4269）和 ggml-org/sesame-csm-1b-GGUF（Issue #9430）。
  11. 质量回归 — Qwen3 推理能力在微调后消失（Issue #3005）；Gemma4-31B-it 退化为重复（Issue #5124）；微调后的 Whisper-large-v3 在波斯语上表现不及 base（Issue #2942）。
  12. 其他 Studio 故障 — 数据集下载失败（Issue #9775）、macOS 文本编码错误（Issue #8594）、qwen2.5 衍生模型上的 LoftQ 训练错误（Issue #6958）、OpenCode 无自动加载（Issue #9171）。

今日已合入的安全修复：

  • 将文件链接到聊天的工具工作区时防止跟随符号链接（来自最新安全扫描）——PR #13513。
  • HF 认证 token 不再被 from_pretrained(token=...) 覆盖——PR #13486。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • Browser Use 使 Unsloth 成为可行的本地智能体运行时。 模型现在可以导航，按 ref 或坐标点击、拖拽并运行经批准的脚本 (PR #13505)。如果你构建浏览器智能体，可以将其与 headless-Chrome 技术栈对比评估——但要为上下文再处理回归（#10698）做好预算，它会让当今的长上下文工具循环变得昂贵。
  • 工具调用工作负载现在需要上下文管理策略。 再处理回归加上新的“Context compacted”内联分隔符 (PR #13502) 表明，跨工具轮次的提示缓存尚不可靠。在扩展智能体循环之前，请测量每次工具调用的 TTFT。
  • 多模态服务正在快速扩展。 Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo（8 步）、LTX-2.5 fp8/int8 预量化 DiT 以及文本扩散训练意味着一个运行时正越来越多地覆盖图像、视频和音频管线——audio.cpp 和 whisper.cpp 的更新流程正在被合并到单张卡片中 (PR #13497)。
  • 如果你依赖量化选择，请锁定版本。 Model List API 仍无法表达按量化方案的目标 (Issue #9340)；按仓库和精度解析模型的客户端需要带外映射。
  • 非 CUDA 部署正获得真正关注（PR #13438 中的 NPU/XPU 缓存释放），但 AMD/ROCm 用户仍报告 offload 和扩散分类 bug（#10341、#13328）——请在 ROCm 上显式验证内存行为，而不是信任 offload 开关。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-13

Generated: 2026-10-13 03:08 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Ecosystem

Digest window: 2026-10-13 · Projects: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth

Counting note: "Issues" and "PRs" below are items surfaced in the 24h digest, not repository totals. They include open bugs, closed items, feature requests and roadmaps, so treat them as an activity indicator, not a defect count.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The datacenter serving tier (vLLM, SGLang, LiteLLM) shipped zero stable releases today, while the local/edge tier moved fast — llama.cpp landed 11 builds in a single window and both Ollama and Unsloth pushed betas. Effort is concentrated on a narrow set of frontier MoE architectures (DeepSeek-V4/4.1, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.x, Gemma4), and the most consequential in-flight engineering is multi-adapter/MoE LoRA serving (SGLang's 21-part runtime stack) and prefill-decode disaggregation as the default scale-out topology. The dominant risk theme is speculative decoding, which is simultaneously the most actively optimized and the least stable feature across vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp. Hardware breadth keeps expanding (AMD gfx942/gfx950/MI355X, Intel XPU/Arc, Ascend NPU, Apple MLX, Hexagon, AMX), but backend correctness bugs — duplicate expert IDs, FP8 load gaps, MLX kernel panics — are the recurring tax.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release status
vLLM Datacenter serving engine ~21 ~14 No release — latest release list empty
SGLang Datacenter serving engine ~27 ~20 (incl. 21-part LoRA stack #42880–#42888) No release
llama.cpp Local/edge GGUF runtime (ggml) ~19 ~23 11 builds: b11567–b11577
Ollama Local runtime + cloud product ~26 ~17 v0.40.4-rc0
LiteLLM LLM gateway / proxy ~24 ~14 No release
Unsloth Fine-tuning + Studio runtime ~29 ~15 v0.1.906-beta

Reading the table: issue-heavy counts for Ollama and Unsloth reflect active defect/regression backlogs rather than forward feature velocity. llama.cpp's same-day issue-to-PR ratio (~19:23) indicates the healthiest fix-throughput; SGLang is landing the largest single feature body (LoRA runtime) in staged parts.

3. Model Support Race

Project New architectures / models landed Notable gaps (requested or broken)
vLLM Clef-Flash native support via /v1/systemone (Qwen3.5 backbone + joint schema head); DeepGEMM 26/09/30 bump for DSv4 sparse indexer; NVFP4 per-forward W4A4/W4A16 for SM120/SM121 routed experts DeepSeek-V4-Flash unrunnable on SM8x (#50576); GLM-5.3-Flash no sparse-MLA on sm_89 (#54059); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 fails to load on ROCm (#58688); Gemma4 sequence classification (#43726); Qwen3.5-397B PD disaggregation (#43765)
SGLang GLM-5.3-Flash (colocated prefill-attention CP + decode/verify TP, native MTP, DFlash2); DeepSeek-V4.1 TP2 decode fusions (fused all-reduce + mHC epilogues, fused inverse-RoPE + WO-A + MXFP8, SM100 swap-AB attention); MiniCPM-V 4.7 cookbook; NVFP4 MoE LoRA on Marlin; XPU prefill graph; NPU prefill CP AMD DSV4.1 sparse decode broken by upstream aiter API removal (#43765, closed without fix path)
llama.cpp vLLM d3 / "pplx-decider" (b11572) and d2 (b11571) with stricter tensor-name validation; same-day multi-sequence fix (b11577); Hexagon Q1_0 HVX MUL_MAT; Intel Arc Pro B65; multi-node TP via NCCL; RPC supports_op negotiation Failling MTP/DFlash2 drafts under --split-mode tensor; Vulkan MUL_MAT_ID row loss (#29821)
Ollama llama.cpp b11521 → decision models + EmbeddingGemma 2; CLI decision-model support; Prism support (PR open); clef / clef flash cloud; glm-ocr EOT fix Prism ternary GGUFs (PQ2_0/PTQ1_0) import failures (#18521); K2 Horizon family requested (#18698)
LiteLLM No new model/hardware integration; cost-parity tests for gpt-6 / Claude 5 bridge; Gemini context-cache creation tokens now billed Bedrock autodiscovery request closed unfixed (#43568)
Unsloth Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo (8-step image gen); LTX-2.5 fp8/int8 from pre-quantized DiTs; text-diffusion LLM training; faster MoE GGUFs; speculative decoding Ling 3.0 in Studio (#8532); Gemma4e2b on Windows (#13388); MLX pretraining structure (#8607)

Who's ahead:

  • SGLang leads on frontier-MoE deployment depth — it is the only project shipping production decode fusions for DeepSeek-V4.1 at TP2 and full GLM-5.3-Flash attention topology.
  • vLLM has the broadest model and hardware matrix, plus the only native new-architecture landing today (Clef-Flash) and forward NVFP4 precision-switching.
  • llama.cpp has the fastest architecture intake velocity for local serving — two new architectures plus a correctness fix inside one window.
  • Unsloth owns the generative-multimodal lane (image/video) that no serving engine in this set covers natively.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort is split across six distinct battlegrounds:

KV cache & prefix reuse — the weakest link, and the one agent workloads hit hardest.

  • vLLM: HIT_PENDING has no deadline, stalling requests until client timeout (#49829); long-prefill defer mode (#61080) and adaptive prefill budget RFC (#52906) target tail latency.
  • SGLang: EAGLE spec-decode KV index rebuilds now parallelized for the 90k–170k KV-token regime (#42803) — explicitly a long-context win. Critically, both agentic KV-reuse proposals (#27574, #30928) went inactive, leaving RadixAttention's byte-identical prefix matching as the only mechanism.
  • llama.cpp: new ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback (b11567) makes mid-inference buffer re-reservation observable — a real p99 diagnosability upgrade.
  • Unsloth: full-context reprocessing after every tool call (#10698) — minutes of stall at ~30k tokens.

Quantization / low precision — where the headline numbers live.

  • vLLM: NVFP4 MoE per-forward W4A16→W4A4 switching (#54617); but FlashInfer NVFP4 causal prefill is 1.7–1.8x slower than FP8 on SM120 (#50416).
  • SGLang: FP8 MoE LoRA Triton vendor (#42885), CuTeDSL FP8 tile tables tuned for B200, GB300, H200 (#42887), NVFP4 MoE LoRA on prepared Marlin weights (#42888).
  • llama.cpp: +13% token generation on AMX Q4_K decode with bit-identical output (#30429) — the cleanest adoptable win today; Q2_K VGPR spill fix for gfx906/MI50 (#29910).
  • Unsloth: LTX-2.5 avoids quantizing a 38 GB bf16 transformer at load, cutting peak memory and startup cost.

Kernels / fusion — abundant but narrow. vLLM's mamba gather fusion (7 Triton kernels → 1, ~6x) and DFlash padding (35.8 µs/step) are explicitly isolated kernel microbenchmarks, not end-to-end throughput claims. SGLang's proposed monokernel framework (#43949, persistent kernels covering most of a decoder layer in 1–2 launches) is the most ambitious structural idea in flight.

Distributed / parallel serving — SGLang's Q4 PD-disaggregation roadmap (#43699) positions PD as the mainstream deployment shape; heterogeneous TP KV transfer now handles hybrid SWA models (gpt-oss-120b, TP1 prefill / TP4 decode, #40909); prefill CP is the last open item across MHA/GQA backends (#21788). llama.cpp added multi-node NCCL tensor parallelism (#28967).

Batching & scheduling — vLLM run-batch now streams responses incrementally (frontend memory, #52505); SGLang's bench_serving --request-rate drifts progressively behind schedule (#43930), which skews benchmark baselines.

Speculative decoding — a frontier of its own, with real wins (SGLang EAGLE index parallelism) and real hazards (§6).

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Projects Role and differentiator
Datacenter serving engine vLLM, SGLang GPU-first, multi-GPU/PD-aware, OpenAI-compatible APIs. vLLM competes on hardware/model breadth and is absorbing gateway concerns (opt-in fastapi-guard middleware, #60988). SGLang competes on frontier-model depth, long-context/prefix-heavy workloads and PD disaggregation, and is making the biggest multi-adapter bet. Both are now shipping features that were previously gateway-layer (auth, rate limiting, logging).
Local / edge runtime llama.cpp, Ollama llama.cpp is the engine + ggml backend layer: GGUF, CPU/consumer-GPU/Apple/Hexagon, multi-backend. Ollama is the productized layer on top — model management, CLI, desktop, cloud-hosted models — and explicitly tracks llama.cpp upstream via version bumps (b11521). Ollama now stretches up-stack with cloud models and tool calling.
Gateway / proxy LiteLLM Not an inference engine. Owns cross-provider protocol translation, auth, budgets, cost accounting, and the MCP gateway. Its moat is breadth of provider coverage and billing correctness — not kernel throughput. Directly threatened at the edges by engine-native middleware, but differentiated by cost/observability/MCP depth.
Training / fine-tuning + local app runtime Unsloth Fine-tuning, quantization, GGUF export, and Studio as the app surface. Uniquely spans train → quantize → serve → agent in one stack, and today extended into browser-agent execution and image/video generation. Embeds llama.cpp and vLLM as backends rather than competing with them.

Boundary blurring is the story: engines are adding gateway middleware, Ollama is adding cloud/agent features, Unsloth is adding an agent runtime, and LiteLLM is adding an MCP gateway. Integration surface — not raw kernel speed — is where the layers are colliding.

6. Trend Signals

  1. DeepSeek-V4 / frontier MoE is the single integration battleground. Every serving project is spending its highest-signal cycles there, and AMD is consistently the last platform supported (SM8x gap, gfx950 sparse-decode break, MI355X trackers).
  2. Speculative decoding is the highest-risk production feature in the ecosystem. Three of four runtimes report it as a top instability source: SGLang's server-killing SIGKILL on any temperature > 0 (#43412), GLM-5.3 + DFLASH silent quality collapse (#40843); llama.cpp divergence on quantized targets (#25618) and PP halving on multi-GPU splits (#27428); Unsloth's draft paths; vLLM's DFlash/DSpark acceptance collapse under prefix caching (#47930).
  3. Multi-LoRA / multi-adapter serving is the next unlock — and it will cause churn. SGLang's 21-part stack (MoE LoRA across Triton, CuTeDSL, Marlin for FP8/NVFP4/BF16) is the largest feature landing anywhere. Meanwhile vLLM has an open CUDA-graphs deadlock with fused-MoE LoRA + --fully-sharded-loras (#60845). Plan evaluation, not adoption, this quarter.
  4. Agentic workloads have outrun engine KV capabilities. Position-independent and programmatic KV reuse proposals are dead in SGLang; engines still depend on byte-identical prefix matching. Practical mitigation today is prompt-stability engineering (fixed prefixes, ordered tool schemas) — plus awareness that llama.cpp's RAM-backed prompt cache can leak content across conversations under concurrent load (#27148), a data-isolation issue for multi-tenant servers.
  5. Multi-tenancy and billing correctness are now infrastructure concerns. LiteLLM's v1.93.0 Redis failure breaks caching and budget counters (#34614), v1.92's missing budget_fallbacks column blocks Admin UI (#33074), and a proxy-admin JWT previously bypassed personal max_budget (#41226). Unsloth patched symlink-following into chat tool workspaces and an HF token-clobbering bug.
  6. Hardware diversification is real but fragile. AMD gfx942/gfx950, Intel XPU/Arc B65, Ascend NPU prefill CP, Apple MLX, Hexagon HVX, Arm AMX all saw activity — yet the AMD DSV4.1 break came from an upstream aiter API removal outside SGLang's control, and MLX SDPA panics block Ollama on Apple Silicon.
  7. Release cadence is bifurcating. Datacenter and gateway tiers shipped nothing stable; local/packaged tiers shipped betas and 11 llama.cpp builds. Pin-and-benchmark discipline is mandatory: Ollama carries a reported 25–30% throughput regression vs v0.40.1 (#18968), and LiteLLM's advisories make v1.93.0/v1.92 unsafe defaults.

What to watch as an agent/application developer:

  • Measure TTFT per tool call before scaling agent loops — Unsloth's reprocessing regression (#10698) and the universal KV-reuse gap both surface here.
  • Validate speculative decoding on your exact install method (pip bundle vs. container vs. source) with sampled traffic, and diff against a non-speculative baseline on quantized targets.
  • Treat kernel-level benchmarks as directional only — vLLM's 6x mamba fusion and 35.8 µs DFlash saving are isolated measurements; demand end-to-end numbers.
  • Track SGLang's PD-disaggregation roadmap (#43699) and vLLM's long-prefill defer mode (#61080) if you operate long-context or tail-latency-sensitive fleets.
  • Watch whether engine-native middleware (fastapi-guard in both vLLM and SGLang) erodes the standalone-gateway tier — relevant if you're standardizing on LiteLLM for auth and rate limiting rather than for cost/MCP/protocol translation.
